name: @clay-design-system/mcp

tools.name: clay_search
tools.description: Ask the Clay design system a question; returns the top record ids with summaries (BM25 + facets, plus meaning-based matching when semantic search is installed). Follow up with clay_get. Use `each` to resolve several names (logos, icons, sections) in one call. Tokens, icons, logos and shapes rank below prose unless you pass `kind`: use kind ["token"] for a color, spacing or radius value, ["icon"] or ["logo"] for assets; without it a token question returns no token.

query.description: Words to search for. Required unless `each` is given.

each.description: Several names to resolve in one call (logos, icons): the best hit per term; `query`, if set, is added to each.

k.description: How many hits (default 10; with `each`: per term, default 1).

kind.description: Record kinds or subkinds, e.g. gotcha, policy, layout, limit, rule, section, token, logo, icon. Pass ["token"] when the answer is a design token.

stage.description: Only records that apply to these stages.

mode.description: web-compose mode: A = page brief, B = PMM brief (structure and copy already decided).

scope.description: Default web + ds + shared; email knowledge needs ["email"] (or ["all"]).

detail.description: Per hit: subkind, name, status and links.

json.description: Return the answer as JSON text (same content plus the registry version) instead of Markdown.

tools.name: clay_get
tools.description: Full bodies of Clay records by id, up to 25 ids in ONE call (an id ending in * expands to that prefix). Aliases work: web-pmm, section:FeaturesSection, --clay-web-type-family. Each record has a links line (import path, Storybook, Figma, CDN).

ids.description: One id or up to 25. An id ending in * expands to that prefix.

detail.description: Add the full registry record: columns, aliases, links, relations (50 per direction, with counts), render metadata; recipes and pages add pageRecipe.

json.description: Return the answer as JSON text (same content plus the registry version) instead of Markdown.

tools.name: clay_list
tools.description: Without `kind`: the record kinds and subkinds with counts. With `kind` (a kind or a subkind, e.g. section, token, logo, rule): its records as `id — summary`, paged. Sections: kind=section is every section RECORD (web and email entity sections plus their usage/example/content sub-records), not what a PageSpec takes; for the PageSpec `type` values trust kind="section-type" (same as renderable: true), and entity: true drops the sub-records.

kind.description: A kind or subkind. Omit to list the kinds. "section-type" lists the PageSpec section types (the renderable sections).

scope.description: Only this scope: web, email, ds, shared.

status.description: Only this status, e.g. active, deprecated.

renderable.description: Sections only: just the records that are PageSpec section types (what clay_validate_page and the renderer accept).

entity.description: Sections only: just the entity sections (section.HeaderSection, section.email.hero), no usage/example/content sub-records.

json.description: Return the answer as JSON text (same content plus the registry version) instead of Markdown.

tools.name: clay_related
tools.description: Typed edges of a record, out and in (variant-of, uses-token, uses-component, has-item, composes, …), grouped by type.

id.description: The record. Accepts a record id (section.FeaturesSection), an entity id (section:FeaturesSection), a skill alias (web-pmm), a handbook id or a CSS variable (--clay-web-type-family).

type.description: Only these relation types, e.g. uses-token, variant-of, has-item.

kind.description: Only edges whose other end has one of these kinds or subkinds.

json.description: Return the answer as JSON text (same content plus the registry version) instead of Markdown.

tools.name: clay_asset_url
tools.description: The CDN URL of a logo, icon, badge, agent image or shape (`id → url`), and for a customer or integration logo its PageSpec logo key (what `logoKeys` / `logoKey` take; renderPageSpec resolves keys, never URLs). Takes a record id, a PageSpec key (customers/canva-default, integrations/slack) or a bare name (canva, slack, calendar). A logo family resolves to the file in `variant` (default: the default file). Use `ids` for many.

id.description: One asset: a record id (asset.logo.customer.adevinta, asset.icon.calendar), an alias, a PageSpec logo key (customers/adevinta-default) or a bare name (adevinta).

variant.description: A logo variant (white, black, default, …); an unmatched variant gives no url rather than another colour.

detail.description: For a logo family: every variant with its url.

json.description: Return the answer as JSON text (same content plus the registry version) instead of Markdown.

tools.name: clay_render
tools.description: What a section, layout, component or email renders to: the stored render rows (variant, theme, story, checks, screenshots, mirror, version), prerendered by the registry release build from the Storybook stories (reference output, not a page: a page is a PageSpec rendered by renderPageSpec). `variant` is the story name or its slug (Split Full Image = split-full-image). `html: true` adds the HTML (capped at 60 kB). The HTML loads its images from the CDN (dapulse-res.cloudinary.com). An empty answer says why (a registry from before renders shipped, a database built without them, or a record with no story). To INSERT a section into an existing static HTML/CSS/JS page: `bundle: true` returns its section bundle (canonical HTML, its CSS chunk, the tokens it reads, fonts, vanilla JS with init(root)), each file with its sha256 and a version-pinned URL, plus the dependency closure; `integration: true` returns where the CSS and JS go, the token-root and dedupe rules and how to init. With `bundle`, `variant` picks the layout (default: the default layout), `version` pins the release.

id.description: The record. Accepts a record id (section.FeaturesSection), an entity id (section:FeaturesSection), a skill alias (web-pmm), a handbook id or a CSS variable (--clay-web-type-family).

variant.description: Only this variant (e.g. a layout name). With `bundle`: the layout to bundle.

html.description: Include the render HTML (capped at 60 kB; beyond that the mirror url is given).

bundle.description: Return the section bundle for inserting this section into a static page: manifest, files (sha256, pinned URL) and the dependency closure.

integration.description: Return the integration contract: insertion point, <head> and </body> order, dedupe keys, token root, CSS layering, init(root), what to verify. Alone it answers with the instructions and the closure only; with `bundle` it adds them to the files.

version.description: Pin: the package version the bundle must be (e.g. 0.18.1). A mismatch is an error, never a silent other version.

files.description: With `bundle`: "inline" (default) = HTML, CSS, tokens and JS in the answer, fonts by reference; "refs" = references only; "all" = fonts too.

json.description: Return the answer as JSON text (same content plus the registry version) instead of Markdown.

tools.name: clay_section
tools.description: Sections and layouts: props, item shapes with their copy limits, layouts with item ranges and what each drops, gotchas. Several at once in ONE call: names ["A","B"] with layouts ["x",""] paired by position (an unknown name is reported, the rest still answer). Common guesses resolve and say so (HeroSection → HeaderSection). No name lists every section with its layouts and which ones are PageSpec section types.

name.description: e.g. FeaturesSection. Omit (and names) to list every section.

layout.description: e.g. tab-cards-carousel. Several layouts may be comma-separated.

layouts.description: Layouts paired with `names` by position (an empty string = none for that section).

detail.description: Add what the section can hold: item types, nested components, media slots.

json.description: Return the answer as JSON text (same content plus the registry version) instead of Markdown.

tools.name: clay_route
tools.description: What do I need for this stage? The ordered, minimal Clay knowledge for one skill × mode × stage (procedure bodies, the policies that decide collisions, brief → layout candidates, ranked gotchas), inlined within a token budget. Call it at the start of every page-build stage. Outside the Clay repo a web route leads with the PageSpec path: the page is a PageSpec validated by clay_validate_page and rendered by renderPageSpec, never hand-written HTML.

skill.description: Skill running the stage, e.g. web-compose, web-pmm, web-assets, web-qa, email-compose (email skills route over the email scope). Aliases work.

mode.description: web-compose mode: A = page brief, B = PMM brief (structure and copy already decided).

briefPath.description: Repo mode only: a brief file inside the repo.

json.description: Return the answer as JSON text (same content plus the registry version) instead of Markdown.

tools.name: clay_rules
tools.description: The Hard Rules and the Critical/Major policies with enforcement that apply to a stage (and mode); scope "email" lists the email rules instead.

mode.description: web-compose mode: A = page brief, B = PMM brief (structure and copy already decided).

scope.description: `email` lists the email rules; web or omitted lists the web ones.

json.description: Return the answer as JSON text (same content plus the registry version) instead of Markdown.

tools.name: clay_check_copy
tools.description: Copy strings checked against the section limits (chars, words, sentences; hard limits are Critical) and against Hard Rule A11 (no copy in capitals: all-caps or mostly-caps strings are Critical; acronyms such as AI, CRM, SSO pass), reported apart from the length result. Both cover the copy fields that carry a limit (headings, descriptions, item titles, quotes, labels). Pass a PageSpec as `spec`. Repo mode also takes a page file (`page`) or TSX text (`source`).

spec.description: A PageSpec object (or its JSON text).

page.description: Repo mode only: a page name (apps/pages/src/pages/<Page>.tsx) or a .tsx path inside the repo.

source.description: Repo mode only: TSX source text of a page.

all.description: List every checked field, not only the ones outside a limit.

json.description: Return the answer as JSON text (same content plus the registry version) instead of Markdown.

tools.name: clay_validate_page
tools.description: The PageSpec contract: `schema: true` returns its JSON Schema (the whole spec, or one section type's props with `type`) and a valid example, so call it BEFORE writing a spec; `spec` checks one before rendering: the schema, unknown section types (the nearest PageSpec types; HeroSection → HeaderSection), each section's props (a missing required prop names the near miss, e.g. an item's `title` where `heading` is required; an unknown prop is a warning because it is dropped, with the PageSpec name it meant, e.g. React `actions` → `ctas`; an error with `strict: true`, which becomes the default in the next minor), the layout-to-content coupling, what the renderer would normalize, Hard Rule C6 (no two muted sections back to back) and Hard Rule A11 (no copy in capitals); broken hard copy limits are warnings. Section `type` must be one of the PageSpec section types (clay_list kind="section-type"). Every finding has a JSON path and a rule id. A valid spec renders with renderPageSpec from @clay-design-system/react/render.

spec.description: The PageSpec to check: { brand?, nav?, sections: [{ type, props }] } as an object or JSON text. Omit it with `schema: true`.

schema.description: Return the PageSpec JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) and a valid example instead of checking a spec.

type.description: With `schema: true`: only this section type's props schema, e.g. HeaderSection.

strict.description: Unknown props are errors, not warnings (default false; it becomes the default in the next minor, once the page builders' real specs pass).

json.description: Return the answer as JSON text (same content plus the registry version) instead of Markdown.

tools.name: clay_components_using_token
tools.description: Which components and layouts use a design token: `id — summary`. Takes a token id, an alias or a CSS variable (--clay-web-type-family, var(--clay-web-type-family)).

token.description: A token id (token.clay-web-type-family), alias (token:--clay-web-type-family) or CSS variable (--clay-web-type-family).

json.description: Return the answer as JSON text (same content plus the registry version) instead of Markdown.

instructions: Clay: monday.com's marketing design system, registry 0.20.1 (schema 1.4.0). Read-only. Pages compose @clay-design-system/react sections, never hand-coded ones; tokens are CSS custom properties, numeric ones unitless: calc(var(--clay-size-16) * 1px). Page build: clay_route per stage; clay_section for props, item shapes, copy limits, layouts; clay_rules for the Hard Rules; clay_search, then clay_get. For a token, icon, logo or shape pass clay_search kind ["token"] / ["icon"] / ["logo"] (else they rank below prose). Batch: clay_section takes names[] + layouts[], clay_get up to 25 ids, clay_search each[], clay_asset_url ids[]. A page is a PageSpec that renderPageSpec (@clay-design-system/react/render) renders, not hand-written HTML: clay_validate_page {schema:true} gives its JSON Schema, {spec} checks it, then clay_check_copy. Section types: clay_list kind="section-type" (hero = HeaderSection). Ids accept aliases (web-pmm, --clay-*). json:true returns JSON.
